12.1 Introduction

Although the hospital primarily follows Ayurvedic principles, certain clinical situations may require allopathic support, including the use of blood or blood components. The hospital shall ensure rational, evidence-based, minimal, and safe use of blood in collaboration with an authorized licensed blood bank.

12.2 Scope This policy applies to:

• Consultants

• Emergency response team

• Nursing staff

• Referral coordinators

• Interns

12.3. Principles of Rational Use

• Blood and blood products shall be used only when medically necessary and when alternative treatment modalities (Ayurveda/Non-blood options) are inadequate.

• The hospital follows a restrictive transfusion strategy unless contraindicated.

• Only licensed blood banks will be used for procuring blood and components.

REFERENCE:

NABH : Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

12.4 Clinical Indications

Blood products are permitted only in the following scenarios:

12.4.1 Packed Red Blood Cells (PRBC)

• Symptomatic anemia not responding to Ayurvedic management

• Hb < 7 g/dL (without major illness or history or < 8 g/dL in chronic disease

• Acute blood loss > 30%

12.4.2 Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP)

• Coagulopathy with active bleeding

• Reversal of warfarin toxicity only under allopathic consultant’s advice

12.4.3 Platelets

• Platelet count < 10,000 without bleeding

• < 50,000 with active bleeding or before invasive procedures

12.4.4 Cryoprecipitate

• Hypo-fibrinogenemia (<100 mg/DL)

• Ayurvedic interventions should be continued alongside, but never replace urgent transfusion when clinically needed

12.4.5 Alternatives to Transfusion

• Ayurvedic Raktavardhak therapies (Mandura, Punarnava, Drakshasava, etc.)

• Basti: Yapan/Raktabasti

• Iron supplementation

• B12/folate therapy

• Oral/IV fluids

• Proper diet and Rasayana therapy

12.5 Pre-Transfusion Process

1. The treating physician justifies transfusion in writing using a Transfusion Request Form.

2. Informed consent explaining:

o Benefits

o Risks

o Ayurvedic alternatives already given

3. Proper patient identification and sample collection.

4. Cross-matching by a licensed blood bank.

5. Emergency blood release follows blood bank protocols.

12.6 Process

• Two-person verification at bedside (doctor + nurse)

• Match patient details with bag details

• Vital signs monitored:

• Before start

• 15 minutes after

• Hourly

• After completion

• Use sterile, appropriate infusion sets

• Infuse within 4 hours

12.7 Management of Transfusion Reactions

If any reaction is suspected:

1. Stop transfusion immediately

2. Maintain IV access with appropriate fluids

3. Notify physician & blood bank

4. Send post-reaction samples

5. Document event in Transfusion Reaction Form

6. Enter in hospital’s adverse event register

7. Participate in Hemo-vigilance Programme of India (HvPI)

12.8 Documentation

• Transfusion Consent Form

• Transfusion Request Form

• Cross-match report

• Blood issue slip from blood bank

• Nursing monitoring sheet

• Final transfusion notes in patient file

12.9 Training Requirements

• Annual training of all clinical staff on:

• Indications for transfusion

• Identification of reactions

• Safe administration

• Documentation

12.10 Audit and Quality Indicators

The hospital monitors:

• Number of transfusions

• Inappropriate transfusion rate

• Transfusion reaction rate

• Wastage rate

• Compliance with consent and documentation

• Monthly review in Clinical Committee.

12.11 Compliance with Legal Requirements

• Hospital shall NOT store blood without license

• All units are procured from licensed blood banks

• All processes comply with:

• Drugs & Cosmetics Act and Rules

• NABH Guidelines

• NACO & HvPI
